result.title: SemaNorm: Stain Normalization via Semantic and Morphology Alignment for Robust Cross-Hospital Computational Pathology
result.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM) 2026
result.summary: Stain variability remains a major source of domain shift in computational pathology, yet existing normalization methods largely optimize color consistency without explicitly preserving morphology or diagnostic semantics. We propose SemaNorm, a self-supervised stain canonicalization stain normalizer to recover clean patches from strongly perturbed inputs, avoiding paired transfer, adversarial instability, and identity collapse. It further combines a frozen pathology foundation-model consistency loss with a differentiable nuclei-structure loss to preserve semantic and cellular organization. SemaNorm is evaluated across Camelyon17-WILDS and NCT-CRC-HE-100K using cross-hospital tumor classification, cell-graph morphology metrics, and semantic stability measured with an independent held-out foundation encoder. SemaNorm improves out-of-distribution accuracy by 5.9% over the strongest normalization baseline and by 13.5% over no normalization, while achieving the best morphology preservation. Independent foundation-model and cell-graph analyses further confirm improved semantic and structural stability. These results establish morphology- and semantics-aware optimization as a principled alternative to color-only stain normalization.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SemaNorm，一种自监督的染色归一化方法，通过从强扰动输入恢复干净 patch，并结合冻结病理基础模型的一致性损失与可微细胞核结构损失，以同时保留诊断语义与形态结构，在跨医院分类与形态、语义稳定性指标上优于颜色一致性基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「扰动—恢复」训练范式以及用冻结基础编码器作一致性约束来防止语义漂移的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 训练中如何监督视觉证据在内部状态中不坍缩；与原论文的像素级归一化不同，尚需判断该约束能否迁移到 latent 表示。
